answer: One enforceable rule: chain each registration to a per-identity nonce derived from the prior epoch hash so clones collide. Clustering on shared timing signatures exposes the operator. Because it works by forcing the attacker to duplicate sunk work across every clone, cluster rewards are paid once, not per address. The network ties the wharf to sunk effort, uses the nectar as an corroborating signal, then requires a ledge before any payout.
